description:
RAISED BY USER s333 ("we don't create a binary of the runtime for running those?").  Correct — we do
not, and only `tools/prove-core` does.

MEASURED s333: `sbcl --load cl/pcl-runtime.lisp --quit` = **1.17 s wall, 107 MB peak RSS**, paid on
EVERY spawn.  Both hot runners load the runtime from SOURCE per file:
  - sweep-perl-tests.pl:152  `sbcl ... --load $runtime --load $testlib ...`
  - tools/run-dist-t.pl:66   `sbcl ... --load $root/cl/pcl-runtime.lisp --load $lisp`
`tools/prove-core` already has the pattern: build a FRESH core once per invocation into a mktemp
file (trap-removed on exit, so it can never be stale), then `--core` it; header claims ~0.003 s
start vs ~1.2 s compile, and the Pl/t gate goes 8:18 -> 2:30 with it.

WHY IT IS NOT MAINLY A SPEED ITEM (do not sell it as one): 101 board files / 8 jobs saves only
~15 s of wall clock.  The payoff is MEMORY and FLAKINESS:
  - 107 MB of transient COMPILER heap per spawn x 8 concurrent jobs ~= 850 MB that exists only to
    recompile something we already have, on a 13 GB desktop shared with a browser.  s333 lost a
    sweep gate to a system-wide OOM (task #180) — this is a direct contributor.
  - ref.t forks 23 fresh_perl/runperl CHILDREN, each paying 1.17 s + 107 MB again: ~27 s of its
    ~30 s runtime, in a burst of concurrent compiles.  ref.t is exactly the file whose rows flapped
    under memory pressure.  A core may remove the mechanism behind #180's swings, not just soften it.

STEPS: (1) factor prove-core's build-fresh-core-then-run into something the other two runners can
call; (2) wire sweep-perl-tests.pl and tools/run-dist-t.pl to `--core` it, keeping the source path
as a fallback flag; (3) the CHILD path matters most — pclperl-for-tests / whatever fresh_perl
children exec must inherit the core too, or the biggest win is lost; (4) re-measure ref.t alone and
a full sweep's peak/min MemAvailable before vs after (that number is the acceptance criterion, per
the s333 review-doc §4 ask about recording machine state with the verdict).

GOTCHA: the core must be rebuilt per invocation, never cached across commits — a stale core would
silently test the OLD runtime, which is the same failure class as the checked-in transpiled
artifacts (cl/pcl-pack.lisp at gen v2-30 against a v2-71 compiler).  prove-core's mktemp+trap is
the pattern to copy, not to redesign.</description>
